title: Gender and the invisibility of care on Wikipedia
Gender and the invisibility of care on Wikipedia
text:
Result

Produced a matched dataset linking Honours recipients with existing Wikipedia biographies.

Created a set of comparative charts highlighting differences in biography representation by gender and profession.

Identified strong patterns showing that women in caring professions (health, education, nursing) were less likely to have Wikipedia biographies than women in politics, the judiciary, or sport.

title: Gender and the invisibility of care on Wikipedia
text:
Outcome

Findings were written up as a peer-reviewed article and published in Big Data & Society (July 2023).

Visualisations (produced in R/ggplot2) were included in the final paper and presentation materials.

The project provided a reproducible workflow for linking government recognition systems (Australian Honours) with open knowledge sources (Wikipedia).

title: Gender and the invisibility of care on Wikipedia
text:
Impact

Helped quantify and demonstrate the systemic invisibility of women in caring professions on Wikipedia.

Contributed to academic and public discussions on gender, recognition, and representation in digital knowledge platforms.

Publication has been cited in ongoing research around data bias and visibility in open knowledge.

title: Gender and the invisibility of care on Wikipedia
text:
Reflection

Strength: Data linking and visualisation made an abstract bias visible and easy to communicate.

Challenge: Care-related roles often lack the “notability markers” Wikipedia uses, raising broader questions about how recognition is structured.

Curiosity: While working alongside academic collaborators, I was the one who noticed the unexpected angle around caring professions. This discovery shaped the direction of the project, and I valued how my curiosity complemented the team’s expertise.

Collaboration: Partnering with academics helped me translate this observation into publishable research, showing the value of combining different perspectives.
